messages:
anya: Heads-up — we've got a slow memory-growth signal on canary for long-context workloads. KV residency keeps climbing even when eviction_count spikes. Seen this before?

mike: Hmm. Are evictions correlated with new requests or with periodic background compaction?

anya: It's mostly during long-chat sessions (10k+ tokens). Eviction counter increments but total resident bytes still grow. Looks like fragmentation + reuse failure. :thinking_face:

devon: Can you paste the sampler trace? even a small example helps.

anya: paste: ```
KVStats shard=0 { resident_bytes: 12.3GB, evictions_total: 872, residency_histogram: [0-1s:40,1-10s:200,10-60s:300,60s+:300], frag_ratio: 0.28 }
process rss: 19.1GB
requests: avg_seq_len: 7800, batching: off (single-token streaming)
```

lisa: frag_ratio 0.28 is high. If frag happens on many small fragments we can see resident_bytes rise despite evict counts because fragmentation prevents reuse.

mike: Agreed. Two quick hypotheses: 1) page allocator rounding causing small free slots, 2) eviction policy picks large-frag pages so free space is unusable.

anya: Also noticed kv_lookup_hit_rate ~0.86 but effective_reuse_rate (measured by prefix reuse) is 0.6 — mismatch suggests hits are soft (different keys mapping to same slot?)

devon: We should add two metrics: kv_eviction_reason and kv_free_span_size_histogram. Reason label values: lru, residency_limit, compaction, manual_purge. free_span histogram helps quantify unusable free space.

anya: +1 on reason label. Current counter is just evictions_total without reason or shard. Querying Prometheus is a pain.

mike: I'll draft a dashboard panel: top row: resident_bytes_by_shard, free_spans_percentile (p50,p90,p99), eviction_rate_per_min labeled by reason, reuse_ratio_over_time. Next row: per-workload seq_len vs residency, fragmentation_heatmap.

lisa: For alerts: fire if resident_bytes growth rate > 200MB/10m AND free_spans_p90 > 1MB for 15m. That avoids false positives from warmups.

devon: We should also export per-eviction latency — how long entries stayed before eviction. If many evictions are short-lived it suggests churn. Add metric kv_residency_seconds_bucket.

anya: Implemented quick probe in canary today: added kv_evictions_total{reason,shard}, kv_free_spans_bytes_histogram, kv_residency_seconds_bucket. Deploy is in progress. sre-bot: deploy/canary finished (ok). :white_check_mark:

sre-bot: Canary ready — metrics now visible at http://prometheus/canary/targets

mike: Pulled metrics — interesting: evictions_total has a new dominant label reason="residency_limit" and free_spans_p90 = 2.1MB. frag_ratio still ~0.26.

lisa: That's consistent with allocator not coalescing after eviction. We need compaction path or periodic slab merge.

devon: Short-term mitigation: when free_spans_p90 > 1MB trigger aggressive compaction (background job) on that shard. Longer-term: refactor allocator to maintain a size-classed free list to reduce fragmentation.

anya: I ran a quick perf profile: top cost is page_coalesce() called rarely, and memmove hotspots during compaction. Kernel selection for memmove is fine; it's CPU-bound. We can throttle compaction to spare latency.

mike: For observability, add dashboard panel for "eviction_reason_trend" stacked area and a metric math panel for effective_cache_utilization = resident_bytes - wasted_bytes / resident_bytes.

lisa: Wasted_bytes derived from free_spans histogram: sum(free_span_bytes). Good idea to show a derived percent.

anya: After turning on aggressive compaction for shard-0 canary, resident_bytes slope flattened within 20m. Will keep monitoring overnight. :eyes:

devon: Nice. Follow-up items: (1) add eviction_reason and residency histograms to prod exporters, (2) implement background compaction toggle + telemetry, (3) design allocator size-classes. I'll open a ticket and assign.

mike: Also add a small e2e test that simulates 12k token sessions and measures resident growth < X after 1h. Catch regressions.

anya: Ticket created: infra/1234 — "KV allocator fragmentation: eviction reasons + compaction toggle + dashboards". Assigning devon, review mike.

lisa: Thanks everyone — great triage. We'll iterate on the dashboard panels tomorrow. :rocket:
